title: Evaluation map from the tensor-diagonal base change
statement: Let $k$ be a commutative ring, $L$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $B,C$ commutative $L$-algebras, regarded as $k$-algebras by restriction. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(x\otimes y)(x\prime\otimes y\prime)=xx\prime\otimes yy\prime$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Put $R=L\otimes_kL$ and $D=B\otimes_kC$. Give $D$ its $R$-algebra structure through $\psi:R\to D$, $\lambda\otimes\lambda\prime\mapsto(\lambda1_B)\otimes(\lambda\prime1_C)$, and give $L$ its $R$-algebra structure through $\mu:R\to L$, $\lambda\otimes\lambda\prime\mapsto\lambda\lambda\prime$. There is a unique unital ring homomorphism $\beta:D\otimes_RL\to B\otimes_LC$ such that $\beta((b\otimes c)\otimes\lambda)=(\lambda b)\otimes c$ for all $b\in B,c\in C,\lambda\in L$. No injectivity, flatness, reducedness, finite-generation or field assumption is imposed; zero algebras are allowed.

proof.text: Put $H=B\otimes_LC$, with $L$ acting on the first factor. The map $B\times C\to H$, $(b,c)\mapsto b\otimes_Lc$, is $k$-bilinear: it is additive separately, and for $a\in k$ both $(ab)\otimes_Lc$ and $b\otimes_L(ac)$ equal $a(b\otimes_Lc)$ by $L$-bilinearity and restriction of scalars. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], over $k$, gives a $k$-linear map $q:D\to H$ with $q(b\otimes_kc)=b\otimes_Lc$.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, second proof paragraph tensor identity; explicit evaluation construction using Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product

proof.text:
Give $H$ the $R$-module structure $r\cdot h=\mu(r)h$. For $s,t\in L$ and $b\in B,c\in C$, $L$-balancing in $H$ gives
$$q(\psi(s\otimes_kt)(b\otimes_kc))=(sb)\otimes_L(tc)=st(b\otimes_Lc)=\mu(s\otimes_kt)q(b\otimes_kc).$$
By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], elements of $R$ and $D$ are finite sums of pure tensors: absorb every $k$-coefficient into a factor. Both sides are $k$-bilinear in $(r,d)$, so expanding the finite sums gives $q(\psi(r)d)=\mu(r)q(d)$ for all $r\in R,d\in D$. Thus $q$ is $R$-linear for precisely the stated actions.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, second proof paragraph tensor identity; explicit evaluation construction using Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product

proof.text:
Define $h:D\times L\to H$ by $h(d,\lambda)=\lambda q(d)$, with $H$ carrying the $R$-action from Step 2. This map is additive in each variable. For $r\in R$, the first scalar-linearity equation follows from Step 2, and the second from commutativity in $L$:
$$h(\psi(r)d,\lambda)=\lambda\mu(r)q(d)=\mu(r)h(d,\lambda),\qquad h(d,\mu(r)\lambda)=\mu(r)\lambda q(d)=\mu(r)h(d,\lambda).$$
Thus $h$ is $R$-bilinear for the two actions specified in the statement. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], over $R$, gives an $R$-linear map $\beta:D\otimes_RL\to H$ with $\beta(d\otimes_R\lambda)=\lambda q(d)$, hence $\beta((b\otimes_kc)\otimes_R\lambda)=(\lambda b)\otimes_Lc$.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, second proof paragraph tensor identity; explicit evaluation construction using Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product

proof.text:
The map $\beta$ is additive by construction and sends $((1_B\otimes_k1_C)\otimes_R1_L)$ to $1_B\otimes_L1_C$, so preserves the unit. Write $e(b,c,\lambda)=(b\otimes_kc)\otimes_R\lambda$. Using the multiplications in the statement, for $b,b'\in B,c,c'\in C,\lambda,\lambda'\in L$,
$$\beta(e(b,c,\lambda)e(b',c',\lambda'))=(\lambda\lambda'bb')\otimes_Lcc'=((\lambda b)\otimes_Lc)((\lambda'b')\otimes_Lc').$$
The generating assertion of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] applied twice expresses each element of $D\otimes_RL$ as a finite sum of such $e$: first absorb outer $R$-coefficients into $L$, then expand $d\in D$ into pure $k$-tensors. Explicitly, for finite sums $x=\sum_i e_i$ and $y=\sum_j f_j$ of these generators, distributivity and additivity give $\beta(xy)=\sum_{i,j}\beta(e_if_j)=\sum_{i,j}\beta(e_i)\beta(f_j)=\beta(x)\beta(y)$. Empty sums give the same identity if either element is zero. Hence $\beta$ is a unital ring homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, second proof paragraph tensor identity; explicit evaluation construction using Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product

proof.text: If $\gamma:D\otimes_RL\to H$ is another unital ring homomorphism with the required formula, then $\gamma(e(b,c,\lambda))=\beta(e(b,c,\lambda))$ for every triple. By the finite-sum expression from Step 4, derived from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], additivity gives $\gamma=\beta$. This proves uniqueness among all unital ring homomorphisms, without assuming that a competitor is $R$-linear.
